in_arabic.name: كليمة

in_urdu.name: کلیمہ

data.cultural_impact: The Kalimah is a fundamental part of the Islamic identity. It is the declaration of faith that every Muslim is expected to make. The Kalimah is recited during important Islamic rituals, such as prayer and the pilgrimage to Mecca. It is also a necessary component of other Islamic practices, such as marriage. The fact that the Kalimah is shared by all Muslims, regardless of their ethnic, racial, or national background, is a testament to the power of the Islamic faith in uniting people from diverse backgrounds around common beliefs and values.
data.spiritual_significance: The Kalimah is a declaration of submission to God and a testament to one's belief in the unity of God (Tawhid) and acceptance of Prophet Muhammad as the Messenger of God. Reciting the Kalimah is an act of worship that connects the believer to their Creator and reminds them of their ultimate purpose in life, which is to please God and seek His guidance and mercy. The spiritual significance of the Kalimah is such that it is often referred to as the "key to paradise" and the "door to Islam". By confessing faith in the Kalimah, a person gains entry into the Islamic community and embarks on the path towards spiritual growth and enlightenment.
